model.architecture: InternVL3-2B is a compact vision-language model: an InternViT vision encoder + pixel-shuffle + MLP projector feeding a Qwen2.5-1.5B language decoder.

variants.quantization: Decoder Qwen2.5-1.5B int4 weights (symmetric, blockwise-32 + OCTAV optimal-clipping), input embedding INT8 (externalized section); vision encoder + pixel-shuffle + MLP projector int8 weights; integer compute

recommended.reason: measured on one Galaxy S26 with one binary: GPU 40.41 tok/s decode / 631.0 prefill, peak 736 MB, init 3.7 s (S4 GPU gate 2026-08-25, 1 run) against CPU 34.83-43.67 decode / 132.1-207.9 prefill, peak 1364 MB, init 1.7 s (S7 Android backfill 2026-09-05, 2 cold runs). Same-device CPU control taken: decode is a wash (within 10%); gpu is kept for its prefill advantage (time to first token), a deliberate choice rather than a decode win
card: Use the CPU backend on the desktop.

platform_notes: iPhone 17 Pro rows are carried over from the repository's earlier on-device note (model loads in about 3–4 s); run logs are not retained, so run count and prompt are unknown. The GPU row covers single-image VQA.
Multi-turn text works: follow-up questions about the same image are supported.
Vision-only bundle (no audio tower): bring up the engine with the vision modality only (Modality.textImage / [.vision]); requesting the audio tower (.all) fails at session creation.
Galaxy S26 GPU gate prompt carries no image: it covers engine creation and the text path only; the vision path on the GPU is not measured there.
Galaxy S26 GPU gate: XNNPACK additionally takes 1 of the 4 nodes in `main`; the runtime accepts that split.

measured.source: model card: Performance table (litert-lm benchmark, Apple M4 Max) (card retrieved 2026-09-05)

S4 GPU gate, 205-token benchmark, single run; full delegation (3618 ops across 3 subgraphs); generation gate answered the probe correctly. No same-device CPU control was taken, so this is a GPU speed, not a measured win over CPU.

S7 Android backfill: same-device CPU control - identical binary, prompt file and flags, only --backend differs; 205-token prompt with --benchmark, 2 cold runs (compile/weight caches deleted between runs, device cooled below 42 C before each run); the GPU path does not run for this file on this handset, so this row has no GPU counterpart

known_issues: macOS GPU backend is not usable on litert-lm 0.15.0: with --backend gpu it returns a run of '!' characters instead of a caption; the benchmark still reports 2,031 tok/s prefill / 183 tok/s decode on that unusable path, so no GPU row is quoted. Desktop-runtime observation only.

GPU (Metal) backend: a second image in the same conversation truncates the answer; ask about one image per chat. GPU-delegate-specific, not a model/bundle issue — on the CPU backend multi-image works perfectly (verified); reproduces with FastVLM-0.5B, general to the runtime's GPU fast_vlm path.
